newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Lex plans buys in strategic refocus.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Lex plans buys in strategic refocus.

text.p: UK vehicle distribution group Lex Service Plc said on Friday it planned to bolster its strategic refocusing on high-margin quality car dealerships by making acquisitions and 10 million stg in capital expenditure this year.
In an interview with Reuters, David Leibling, director of corporate communications, said "We plan to invest up to 10 million stg in development and further acquisitions."
He said no specific deal-making budget had been allocated, but added that the sale of Lex's volume car dealerships to Pendragon Plc for 44 million stg gave it some cash to play with.
He said expansion of the specialist car dealership would be be targeted at all the luxury carmakers, including the Mercedes and Jaguar brands.
The decision to sell its volume dealership business meant the group now had "five or six businesses which are all contributing sizeable chunks of profits".
The decision to sell followed the arrival of new chief executive Andy Harrison last year, said Leibling, creating a "broadly based automotive services company".
He said the decision to get out of the volume market which included brands like Ford and Vauxhall cars was triggered by poor market returns.
"The specialist car market gives much healthier returns and historically has done extremely well," said Leibling.
Lex said the car market would grow by around five percent this year, but it added that the recent spate of interest rate hikes may dampen back consumer demand.
The recent July 2 budget had a mildly positive effect due to the reduction in corporation tax, with no specific measures hampering its key markets, said Lex.
